situation: A CSS Grid column is sized with a bare fr track (e.g. grid-template-columns:1fr) at a responsive breakpoint, and new content with an unshrinkable flex row (fixed-shrink buttons/controls alongside flex:1 items) is later added somewhere inside that column
right_direction: Always wrap fr tracks in minmax(0,1fr) (or set an explicit min-width:0 on the track/item), matching the pattern the rest of the stylesheet already used at its OTHER breakpoints. A bare fr track's automatic minimum is 'auto' (= the largest min-content of its contents), so CSS Grid lets the track — and everything in it — overflow the grid container once any descendant's min-content is nontrivial, even many levels of plain block divs below the grid item.
anti_pattern: Assuming overflow at a narrow viewport must be caused by the new element's own CSS (padding/width) and debugging only that element — the actual box only needed min-width:0, which wasn't missing on the new content but on an ancestor grid track several levels up and present before this change.
